● Both done, live-verified against the real remote, pushed to main (546e8d3, 7217ad0).

  labels.nix ──(definition)──► remote label set
                                    │
         remote label not in config │
                                    ▼
                          used by an OPEN issue?
                           ┌────────┴────────┐
                         yes                 no
                          │                  │
                    keep + collect     delete (pool of 8)
                          │                  │
                          └──────► errors ◄──┘ (delete failures)
                                    │
          create/update ▸ lint issues ▸ sync todos ▸ print errors ▸ exit 1
                                    │
                      fingerprint left unsaved ⇒ retried next shell

  - t:feature = #2bd4a0 (checked it adds no new near-color collision; t:enhancement's description narrowed to "Improve something that already works" so the two aren't synonyms).
  - The old delete path was a is_terminal() prompt — i.e. dead code from a shell hook. Replaced by thread::scope + a Mutex work queue (8 workers, no tokio in a -Zscript file); the "? on remote but not in config" drift line is gone since
  deletion now reports itself.
  - Issue list is fetched once and shared with the linter (one fewer API call).
  - Live run on this repo deleted the 14 legacy unprefixed labels (bug, enhancement, wontfix, …) and created t:feature; I then injected a label on open #2 to confirm the blocked path — it kept that one, deleted the free one, printed the
  error, exit 1.

  Trade-offs: a label still on an open issue blocks; closed issues silently lose labels that aren't in the config (that's the requested rule, but it is irreversible history loss — noted in CHANGELOG). If the open-issue list can't be
  fetched, nothing is deleted and it only warns, rather than erroring forever on an issues-disabled repo. PRs aren't scanned for label usage. A legacy bug on an open issue takes two runs to converge (lint migrates it to t:bug after the
  delete pass).

  Side effect: I cleared ~/.local/state/git_ops/labels/* while testing, so every other repo re-runs its label sync once on next shell entry — idempotent, and they're pinned to v1.6 so they still use the old code path.
